edges.description: Gaseous distension and pressure equalization within the esophageal body from unvented air trigger repetitive secondary peristaltic contractions to sweep the trapped gas bolus distally.
Pressurized gaseous distension of the esophagus produces sharp retrosternal chest discomfort.
Unvented gas retained in the upper gastrointestinal tract and returned distally into the stomach and intestines causes progressive abdominal bloating and distension.
Unvented upper gastrointestinal gas that cannot be expelled orally transits the intestinal tract and is expelled as excessive flatus.
Postprandial gaseous distension of the esophagus and stomach triggers nausea.

Hiccups occur as part of the associated R-CPD symptom complex inferred to result downstream of unvented gaseous esophageal and gastric distension, although the intermediate reflex pathway is not directly characterized in the R-CPD literature.
Oscillating intraesophageal gas propelled by secondary peristalsis against a closed upper esophageal sphincter generates audible retrosternal and cervical gurgling noises.

Impaired esophageal body clearance and high rates of ineffective swallows are manometrically associated with R-CPD and may contribute to intraesophageal gas and bolus retention, although causality could also run in the reverse direction from chronic esophageal distension.

evidence.reference_title: Retrograde Cricopharyngeus Dysfunction effectively treated with low dose botulinum toxin. A case report from Italy.
evidence.snippet: A large constellation of hitherto unexplained symptoms including inability to burp, gurgling noises from the chest and lower neck, abdominal bloating, flatulence, painful hiccups and emetophobia was defined as Retrograde Cricopharyngeus Dysfunction (R-CPD) in 2019.

evidence.reference_title: Retrograde cricopharyngeus dysfunction: How does the inability to burp affect daily life?
evidence.snippet: 99% reported inability to burp, 98% reported abdominal bloating, 93% reported socially awkward gurgling noises, 89% reported excessive flatulence.

evidence.reference_title: Etiology, Clinical Presentation, and Management of Retrograde Cricopharyngeus Dysfunction: A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: In addition to the cardinal symptom of the inability to belch, associated complaints of bloating and chest pain, gurgling noises, and excessive flatulence were found in 95.7%, 86%, and 80.2% of cases, respectively.

nodes.description: Injection of botulinum toxin type A (typically 50 to 100 units, with efficacy reported down to 10 units) into the cricopharyngeus muscle via operating-room rigid or flexible esophagoscopy or awake in-office electromyography-guided percutaneous/transtracheal approaches. Temporary chemodenervation relaxes the upper esophageal sphincter, serving as both a confirmatory diagnostic test and definitive therapy that frequently leads to durable reflex retraining beyond the pharmacologic half-life of the toxin.
